rationale: Comprehensive phenotypic analyses of KDM2B-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621474) substantiate that congenital heart defects (CHD) exhibit domain- and variant-dependent penetrance. In the largest evaluated cohorts, individuals harboring missense or intragenic deletions specifically affecting the DNA-binding CxxC zinc-finger domain demonstrated a CHD frequency exceeding 75% (14/18, 77.8% in van Oirsouw et al. 2026, and up to 78% in van Oirsouw et al. 2025). Conversely, individuals with putative loss-of-function (pLOF) variants showed reduced penetrance at approximately 60% (3/5), while contiguous 12q24.31 microdeletions including KDM2B presented with cardiac defects in only 25% (3/12, dropping below 30%). While independent smaller series (such as Gomes et al. 2026, reporting ASD/VSD in 2 of 3 CxxC cases) show slight cohort variation, no published literature refutes the observed cardiac burden disparity across these variant types.

evidence.text: In a comprehensive cohort assessment, congenital heart defects were identified in 14 of 18 (77.8%) individuals with KDM2B CxxC domain variants, 3 of 5 (60%) individuals with loss-of-function variants, and 3 of 12 (25%) individuals with contiguous 12q24.31 microdeletions.

new_directions.question_text: Does dominant-negative interference or gain-of-function by CxxC-mutant KDM2B account for the heightened cardiac penetrance compared to pure haploinsufficiency?
new_directions.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. (2025) demonstrated that mutant KDM2B proteins with CxxC alterations are stably expressed in vitro but show impaired DNA binding and distinct subepisignatures, suggesting a non-haploinsufficient mechanism that may dysregulate cardiogenic transcriptional programs more severely than loss-of-function alleles.

new_directions.question_text: What modifier genes within the 12q24.31 contiguous deletion locus or compensatory transcriptional pathways explain the lower penetrance of congenital heart defects in deletion carriers compared to point mutations?
new_directions.rationale: Contiguous deletions typically result in more severe phenotypes, but in KDM2B/12q24.31, CHD is reported in only 25% of microdeletions versus ~78% in CxxC missense variants, suggesting deletion may not trigger the specific aberrant chromatin-binding dynamics of CxxC point mutants.
